# derived from monero v0.18.5.1 source and DESIGN.md §5b, not captured from a run
# Expectation for `history_cache_fresh` against input/history.bin. See
# tests/fixtures/doctor/history_cache_fresh/expect.json for the FMONERO_CACHE_DIR seam, the byte-by-byte
# header layout, why the file is a header with no body, and why the class is D.
#
# THIS CASE: THE MAGIC IS WRONG. One byte differs from the base case:
#   46 4d 48 59   b"FMHY" instead of 46 4d 48 58   b"FMHX"
# Everything after it -- version, fingerprint, high_water, built_at -- is byte-identical to the fresh
# case, so this fixture isolates the magic and nothing else. It stands in for the three header mismatches
# §5b treats identically: a wrong magic, a format_version from a different build (postcard is not
# self-describing, so a bumped version means the BODY's layout changed and the old bytes cannot be
# decoded), and a wallet_fp from a DIFFERENT WALLET.
# THAT LAST ONE IS WHY THE FINGERPRINT EXISTS, and it is a money-adjacent guarantee rather than a
# performance one: without it, opening wallet B would serve wallet A's cached transfer rows -- other
# people's addresses, amounts and notes, under wallet B's name. §5b sizes it honestly: the first 16 bytes
# of sha256(primary_address), which "only has to notice that this is a different wallet, it is not
# resisting an adversary", and the address it hashes is public (§2b).
# THE RULE §5b STATES, AND THE ONE THING THIS CASE MUST PROVE: "A header mismatch is STALE, NOT CORRUPT:
# ignored and refetched, NEVER AN ERROR." So history::header must return a CacheHeader with magic_ok
# false -- the field exists for exactly this -- rather than Err, `wallet history` must still work by
# refetching, and the doctor must report rather than complain. A detector that maps a bad magic to Err
# breaks a read-only command on a file the code is designed to discard.
# status `warn`, severity `info`, class D, `fixable` false -- as in the __stale case, and STATUS IS PHASE
# 0'S READING for the same reason: §7.1 fixes severity, class and fixability but not the status for a
# mismatched header.
# THE DETAIL MUST SAY WHICH PART DID NOT MATCH -- magic, version or fingerprint. They have different
# meanings to a user ("corrupt or foreign file", "upgraded fmonero", "this is another wallet's cache")
# even though §5b gives all three the same treatment, and `fmonero wallet history --limit 1` is the fix
# for all three.
# NOTHING HERE NEEDS A DELETE, which is §7's argument in miniature: the next `wallet history` overwrites
# the file through history.bin.tmp.<pid> + rename(2), so a doctor that could delete it would be a doctor
# with a RemoveFile Action -- backup, hash pair, recorded inverse, undo path and fixture -- to undo
# removing a file the code replaces unprompted.
